title: Scrambler
description: Turtle and back-exposure reversals for turning defensive scrambles into top position.

media.title: JOZEF CHEN revolutionizing turtle "Stop Giving Up Your Back! Turtle Escape & Back-Exposure System
notes: Context: Jozef shows an open-turtle approach that uses one knee to chest and one knee away to make the hook threat more predictable, then turns that read into a hip-switch reversal.
- [00:12-00:32] Play one knee to chest and one knee away so the hook threat is forced to one side.
- [00:42-01:00] Monitor the cradle hand and protect your chin before switching your hips.
- [01:01-01:30] Hip-switch when their weight commits to your hips, clear their knee off your hip, then knock them down.
- [01:32-01:45] Control the high leg to stay on top; if it retracts, expect to transition into front headlock or a scramble.
- [01:46-02:10] If you cannot get behind them, shoot deep to a seatbelt, emphasize shoulder position, and shoulder-roll to expose the back.

media.title: ESCAPE the Back EVERY Time - High-Crotch Counter to Hooks (BJJ Back Defense)
notes: Context: this is the specific Kenta Iwamoto hook-entry counter. It fits inside the broader turtle system when they are behind you and start inserting a hook to take the back.
- [00:02-00:16] Protect one side and anticipate the hook before it settles.
- [00:16-00:23] Build an underhook/high-crotch grip as the hook comes in.
- [00:23-00:45] Option 1: pull up, post your hand, pin their hip to the floor, then shelf the leg or roll through to secure position.
- [00:46-01:09] Option 2: if their weight blocks the hip pin, lift, put your hips underneath their legs, and sneak out from the back side.

media.title: 3 back escapes I tested over years of trial and error
notes: Context: Rau covers three common back-escape scenarios, including high-ball ride, turtle with no hooks, and back-triangle threats.
- [00:27-01:33] Against the high-ball ride, defend the neck and second hook at the same time: chin to shoulder, eyes toward the armpit, monitor the knee, and toe-knee walk to free the hip.
- [01:40-03:21] From the high-ball ride, use the cutback when their legs stay locked; if they unlock to follow, pummel your leg inside to clear the bottom hook and reach turtle with no hooks.
- [03:23-05:08] From turtle with no hooks, roll over the same-side shoulder while overwrapping the leg and keeping knees to chest, then monitor the hook and come on top or recover guard.
- [07:50-10:18] Against the back-triangle entry, slide down, get your shoulder below the knee, keep weight on the locking leg, turn thumb down/elbow up, and swim through to escape.
- [00:27-10:18] The shared theme is hip/shoulder misalignment plus hook denial, not forcing a single reversal from every back-exposure position.
